entity_resolution.arabic_name: أبو علي، الحسن بن الحسن بن الهيثم

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Basra during the Buwayhid dynasty.
Moved to Cairo under the Fatimid Caliphate; feigned madness to escape Caliph Al-Hakim's wrath over Nile regulation failure and was placed under house arrest.
Released from house arrest following the death of Caliph Al-Hakim; continued independent research near Al-Azhar Mosque.
Died in Cairo at the age of approximately 74.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Initiated systematic optical experiments and draftings of Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics) while under house arrest.
Completed Kitab al-Manazir, establishing the intromission theory of vision and the modern scientific method.
Authored 'Maqala fi Daw al-Qamar' (On the Light of the Moon), demonstrating that the Moon shines by reflected sunlight.
Formulated and solved 'Alhazen's Problem' concerning spherical reflection using conic sections.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Intromission Theory of Optics and Pinhole Camera Dynamics
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Resolving the dispute between Euclidean/Ptolemaic extramission (eye emits rays) and Aristotelian intromission (forms enter eye), and quantifying light propagation geometrically.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: Light rays radiate in straight lines from every point on an illuminated object in all directions and enter the eye to form an image without the eye emitting light.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Ray optics framework combined with controlled physical aperture models (Camera Obscura / Al-Bayt al-Muthlim).
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Constructed a dark room with a small hole admitting light from outside candles to project inverted images on a screen; utilized water-filled glass globes to isolate refraction from reflection.

variables_definition.\\theta_i: Angle of incidence measured relative to the surface normal
variables_definition.\\theta_r: Angle of reflection measured relative to the surface normal

equations.validity_domain: Specular reflection on plane, spherical, cylindrical, and parabolic mirrors
equations.assumptions: Light travels as straight lines in uniform isotropic homogeneous media.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Overthrew 1,000 years of extramission theory, introduced controlled quantitative empirical testing, and laid the foundations for modern optics, influencing Kepler, Bacon, and Descartes.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Lacked precise non-linear formulation for Snell's Law (sine law), relying instead on experimental angular tables for refraction.

physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining the exact point on a spherical mirror where a ray from a fixed light source reflects to reach an observer's eye.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: The point of reflection corresponds to the intersection of a circle representing the mirror boundary and a hyperbola derived from the geometric locus of points maintaining equal angles to source and receiver.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Geometric catoptrics utilizing intersection of conic sections.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Analytical geometric derivation validated using polished spherical metal mirrors and geometric construction.

variables_definition.(x_1, y_1): Coordinates of the light source point
variables_definition.(x_2, y_2): Coordinates of the observer's eye point

equations.validity_domain: 2D plane slice of 3D spherical mirror reflection geometry
equations.assumptions: Reflection follows the law of equal angles on tangential planes.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Provided a geometric solution requiring fourth-degree polynomial operations, driving advances in catoptrics and conic section theory up to Huygens and Barrow.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Solved purely through geometric constructions of conic sections without modern algebraic notation.

students: Sorkhab (Persian student who studied under him in Cairo)
precursors_built_upon: Al-Kindi (pioneered early optics in Islamic world)
Ibn Sahl (discovered law of refraction precursor)
Hero of Alexandria (catoptrics and shortest light path)
